In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah al-Ma'un

It is Meccan... [Note: the text states "مَدَنِيَّةٌ", so it is Medinan], and its verses number seven.

[p-6273]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[1-7] ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ ﴿For that is the one who drives away the orphan,﴾ [al-Ma'un: 2] ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the poor.﴾ [al-Ma'un: 3] ﴿So woe to those who pray,﴾ [al-Ma'un: 4] ﴿who are heedless of their prayer,﴾ [al-Ma'un: 5] ﴿who make a show [of their deeds],﴾ [al-Ma'un: 6] ﴿and withhold small kindnesses.﴾ [al-Ma'un: 7]

﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ That is, [who denies] the reward and punishment of God, and so does not obey Him in His commands and prohibitions. Abu al-Su'ud said: it is an interrogative intended to arouse the listener's eagerness to know the one about whom the speech is directed, and an expression of wonder at him. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), or to every person of understanding. The "seeing" here means knowing.

The fa' (so) in His words, exalted is He, ﴿For that is the one who drives away the orphan﴾ [al-Ma'un: 2] is the answer to an omitted conditional clause, with "dhalika" (that) being the subject and the relative clause its predicate. The meaning is: Do you know the one who denies the Recompense or Islam? If you have not known him, or if you wish to know him, then he is the one who drives away the orphan with a harsh push and rebukes him with an ugly rebuke. It is said: "I pushed so-and-so away from his right," meaning I pushed him away from it and wronged him.

﴿and does not urge the feeding of the poor.﴾ [al-Ma'un: 3] That is, he does not urge others among the well-off to feed the needy and relieve their want; rather, he withholds his effort among the rich from relieving the destitute.

Al-Shihab said: if "ta'am" (food) means "ita'am" (feeding), as al-Raghib said, then it is clear. Otherwise there is an implied elided noun, namely "badhl ta'am al-miskin" (the giving of the food of the poor). Its choice over "ita'am" indicates that it is as if the poor man owns what is given to him, as in His words: ﴿And in their wealth there is a known right﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 24] ﴿for the beggar and the deprived.﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 25] So this clarifies the intensity of entitlement. It also contains an allusion to the prohibition of reproaching the recipient with favours.

Abu al-Su'ud said: if the state of the one who fails to urge others to what is mentioned is such, then what do you suppose the state of one who fails to do so while having the ability?

Al-Zamakhshari said: the knowledge of denying the Recompense was made to be the withholding of charity and the readiness to harm the weak. He means that if he had believed in the Recompense and been certain of the threat, he would have feared God, exalted is He, and His punishment, and would not have undertaken this. So when he undertook it, it was known that he was a denier. How severe is this speech! How frightening is this station! How eloquent it is in warning against disobedience, and that it is worthy of being used as evidence of weakness of faith and slackness in the bond of certainty.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿So woe to those who pray,﴾ [al-Ma'un: 4] ﴿who are heedless of their prayer,﴾ [al-Ma'un: 5] Ibn Jarir said: that is, they are negligent, forgetful of it, through being distracted from it and occupied with other things, and sometimes neglecting it, and at other times neglecting its time. Al-Qashani said: that is, "So woe to them," meaning to those described by these attributes: driving away the orphan and not urging the feeding of the poor; who, if they pray, are heedless of their prayer, because of their veiling from its reality through their ignorance and their absence of presence of heart. The word "al-musallin" (those who pray) is an instance of putting the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, to record upon them that the noblest of their acts and the forms of their good deeds are evil deeds and sins, since they lack what would make them valid, namely presence of heart and sincerity. It is given in the plural form because the intended meaning of "the one who denies" is the category.

﴿who make a show [of their deeds]﴾ [al-Ma'un: 6] That is, they make a show of their prayers before people when they pray, for they do not pray out of desire for reward or fear of punishment; they pray only so that believers may see them and think them to be of them, and so refrain from harming them. The root of "al-mura'a" (showing off) is that you see another and he sees you; it is used to mean acting in front of people so that they will praise them. Al-Shihab clarified this.

﴿and withhold small kindnesses.﴾ [al-Ma'un: 7] That is, what is used to assist people and is spent on their aid, of wealth, goods, and everything that benefits. This is because ignorance governs them, causing them to monopolise benefits and depriving them of contemplation of Divine Unity [al-nazar al-tawhidi] and of belief in the Recompense. So there is no love of the Truth in them, through their inclination towards the perishing world, nor justice in their souls, through their being characterised by vices and their distance from virtues. Therefore they do not help anyone, and so they will never prosper. Thus said al-Qashani.

Note:

The primary and direct subject of these verses is the hypocrites in the time of Prophethood. Secondarily and indirectly, it includes everyone in whom those blameworthy qualities are found, by consideration of generality. The surah is Medinan, and its parallel concerning the hypocrites is His words: ﴿And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to people, and do not remember God except a little﴾ [al-Nisa': 142]. For this reason Ibn Abbas said, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir: They are the hypocrites. They used to show off to people with their prayers when they were present, and abandon them when they were absent, and they would withhold lending from them out of hatred for them, and that is al-ma'un.
